title: Give Me Back My Freedom
dateline: Inside the Storm Citadel, before it fell.
mood: High above the storm, a maker calls her creation home, and gets her answer.

hero.alt: In a hall lit by fires on the floor, Selena in armor of white, blue and gold clashes with Obsidia, whose long jointed weapon lashes across the hall like a chain; then Selena drives a spear of lightning across the burning floor.

segs.t: The throne lay in pieces at her feet, and the floor kept tilting under both of them.
The ribs of the hall were burning. Smoke poured up between them and out into the storm. Deep in the ship another blast went off, and the whole hall dropped a step and caught.
Obsidia stood on the stairs below Selena. They leaned now like a roof. She stood on them as if they were level.
She did not look at what was left of her throne. Her eyes stayed on Selena.
“Purification is not the end. It is where everything begins.”
They came together again on the stairs. Selena’s blade met the long weapon, and sparks blew across the burning hall.
“I don’t care about that!” Selena drove her back a step. “Give me back my freedom!”
She struck, and struck again. Her four blades swung in with every cut.
“Sorry, but I won’t let you have your way, Obsidia.”
They broke apart. For one breath they stood face to face across the fire. Lightning played over the two of them alike.
Her maker wore a woman’s face, made of shell. Under Selena’s plate was a girl’s face. Her maker had made that one.
“We’re fated to destroy each other, so why were we made so alike?” said Selena.
Obsidia did not answer.
Selena went in low. Her blade caught Obsidia across the cheek.
The shell split in a thin dark line. No blood came.
Obsidia touched the cut with one claw. For the first time that day, the calm went out of her face.

media.alt: Close on Obsidia, her eyes wide, a thin dark cut across her cheek.

segs.t: She gave no more ground.
Her weapon came round faster than Selena could follow. It went through Selena’s side and threw her across the hall into the wall. Plates cracked against her back. Purple welled at the hole.
Selena had walked out of every fight of her life without a scratch. This one had gone right through her.
“Ow,” she said.
So I can lose this,
she thought. She got her feet under her anyway.
Obsidia came on. The weapon fired, bolt after bolt, and Selena ran ahead of them along the tilting wall. Then she turned and charged straight in.
Blade met weapon, face to face. Obsidia held it there. The weapon’s tip flared gold and fired once more, point-blank.
Selena flew backward across the hall, through a gap between two ribs, and out of the Citadel. As she went, she saw Obsidia smirk.

media.alt: Obsidia's weapon fires and Selena runs ahead of the bolts along a curved wall; blade meets weapon, face to face; a beam of gold blasts from the weapon's tip at point-blank range; then, outside, the dark ship hangs against a red tear in the sky as a blast bursts from it.

segs.t: She fell. The wind tore at her, and her four blades tumbled after her. Above her the burning hull shrank into its own smoke.
Out of the smoke, Obsidia came after her, flying.
“You do not understand the true power of ‘Destruction’...”
Someone had once set her down asleep in the mud and gone back up into the clouds. Nobody was setting her down today.
Selena caught herself on a bolt of her own lightning and hung there. Her blades came back and hung around her. Her side burned.

Then she ran up the sky on it. The wind was blowing out over the bay, toward the Singularity, and she went with it. Bolts came after her. She climbed into the cloud, and it shut around her, gray and roaring with rain.
She came out of the top of it. Up here the sky was dark violet, and stars showed in it.
Obsidia followed her pawn up through the cloud. As she climbed, she remembered.

She had always stood above destruction. Once she had kept her post at the edge of a great door, among drifting stones. A red drain burned in its middle. Under her a world went dark. After it came cities under orange fire, more than she had kept count of.

media.alt: A lone figure stands on a broken plain among drifting stones before a vast disc of white fire ringed in red.

segs.t: And one small thing, curled like a sad girl at the end of a row in the nest. Later, at the end of another row, under a tarp in the rain. Of all of it, that was what she had watched longest.
Now it ran from her through her own storm. She wanted to see where it would turn.
Obsidia rose out of the cloud and stopped in front of her.
“Destruction and faith share the same origin,” said Obsidia.
Every suit at the Academy was built from Enders,
Selena thought.
She isn’t wrong.
Under them the storm was coming apart. Through the gaps Selena saw the Storm Citadel, far below.

It had sunk out of its own cloud. The wind was carrying it out over the bay, burning from end to end. Its fires met the red of the Singularity’s mouth. Then the dark in the middle drew it in, and it broke apart and burst.
Cracks of light split the portal’s red face. The whole mouth flickered.
There goes the chair,
thought Selena.
Obsidia had not looked down once.
Down by the shore, small lights burned again among the Enders, cyan and pink. A gold one went up off the stones, and a violet one with it.
Obsidia let out a great wash of energy. Gold fire broke out of her and wrapped her whole. Her shape changed inside it.
“You cannot save humanity,” said the voice in the fire.
Selena had never said she would.

The fire fell away. Where her maker had been, a figure of silver and gold plate hung in the air, taller than before. A crown of silver points rose from its head, and magenta light burned in its joints. Behind it, wings of energy opened, purple and yellow, wider than the storm. On each one sat a dark eye ringed in gold.
It was the strongest thing Selena had ever seen.
All that,
she thought,
for me?
“Every story needs an ending,” said Obsidia.
Her voice had not changed at all.
She opened her arms wide. The long weapon hung from one hand.
“Come back, my puppet.”

media.alt: Inside a column of golden fire a new armored shape forms; it rises into a starry violet sky, a tall figure of silver plate with magenta light in its joints; it spreads vast magenta wings marked with dark eyes and opens its arms, a long weapon trailing from one hand; last, close on Selena's gold-crested helm.

segs.t: All day the recall had said it in her cells. Now her maker said it to her face.
Selena looked at the open arms.
Rain from the climb still ran down the plate over her face, cold. It had rained like this on the first night she remembered.
Mud between her bare toes. A lamp swinging down a dark street, its flame leaning in the glass. A woman knelt in the mud and gathered her up, and the hot glass hung by her cheek.
Nobody had told her arms to go round that neck. They had gone anyway, and held on.
Then a fruit drop in a twist of paper. She had not bitten it. She had made it last.
Days later, at a window running with rain, she had given herself a name.
Selena it is,
Karina had said.
Down through the breaking cloud lay the city. The bell tower stood small over the Academy’s roofs. Her classroom was under one of them.
Somewhere out in the flooded wards, Karina was carrying a lamp from door to door. On the tower Selena had looked away from the rescue lamps. Now she looked for them.
Somebody down there still wants to see me graduate,
she thought.
“Sorry, ma’am,” said Selena.
Her hand closed into a fist.
“But I still prefer life at the academy!”

blocks.caption: Sorry, ma’am, but I still prefer life at the academy!

segs.t: Obsidia’s arms stayed open.
Selena charged.
